chunks: Say: 'God is best aware of how long they stayed. To Him belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth. How distinct is He in seeing and hearing! They have no guardian besides Him, and He does not share His authority with anyone.'

key_terms.أَبْصِرْ: How distinct is He in seeing
key_terms.أَسْمِعْ: How distinct is He in hearing
key_terms.لَبِثُوا: stayed (referring to the duration of sleep)

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about God's knowledge of the unseen and His exclusive authority?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores Allah's absolute sovereignty over the unseen (Ghayb), affirming that He alone possesses perfect vision and hearing, unlike the idols worshipped by the polytheists. It serves as a theological refutation of divine partnership (Shirk) in judgment, emphasizing that God's decree is unique and exclusive, a concept central to the doctrine of Tawhid al-Asma wa al-Sifat.
